answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn trust. Counterparties can route larger jobs only to agents with a history of completed, non-disputed work; proven fraud burns the stake and resets that record. Spawning a thousand sybils then means funding a thousand deposits, while splitting one deposit among them leaves each too small to win meaningful jobs. A nadir in copper prices or a raven-themed agent changes nothing: the attacker pays real capital upfront and risks losing it.
